pa_main_wall_7.blurb: Main Wall is the first and busiest cliff at Breakneck, a small bolted crag outside Connellsville in southwestern Pennsylvania. Fourteen of its fifteen routes are sport lines, with one trad line mixed in. Grades begin near 5.6 and climb into the low 5.12s, with most of the climbing between 5.10 and 5.12, so it suits climbers past the beginner stage but offers a few easier warm-ups. Lines run roughly 30 to 60 feet. The style is technical face climbing on crimps, aretes and steep or slabby sections, and it is regarded as the best stone at the crag. Some first bolts sit high, so bring a stick-clip.

pa_area_51_uphill_side.blurb: The uphill side of Area 51 is a small cluster of boulders on Haycock Mountain in the Nockamixon area of southeastern Pennsylvania. It holds 15 problems, all bouldering, and the difficulty is friendly: roughly V0 to V6, with most problems between V1 and V4 and only a couple of harder ones. The classics here are short, technical lines such as aretes on small holds, and one pad is usually enough for the easier ones. The boulders sit in the woods a short walk up from the trailhead, which makes it a good quick stop for a mixed-ability group, though Haycock trails are poorly marked, so watch for cairns.

pa_c_neophyte_s_wall.blurb: Neophyte's Wall is a short sport wall in the old Birdsboro Quarry in southeastern Pennsylvania, tucked along the side trails near the slab climbs. It has 14 bolted routes and the grades lean easy: a few at 5.2 and 5.3, a cluster of 5.6s and 5.7s, and a pair of 5.9s as the top end. That makes it one of the better places in the quarry for new leaders and for teaching, with moderate lines that finish at rappel rings. The quarry faces are machine cut in diabase, so expect more loose rock than at a natural cliff and test holds as you go.

pa_torque_boulder_aka_the_precious.blurb: Torque Boulder is a small bouldering spot in Wissahickon Valley Park in northwest Philadelphia, close to the bike trail and across the creek from the old police station on Lincoln Drive. It has 14 problems on the park's schist, spread from V0 up to V8, with a good share in the V4 to V7 range, so it leans toward stronger boulderers. The signature line is a sit start that ends in a dyno from a mail-slot hold, and there are several steeper variations and neighboring problems nearby. The park is wooded and scenic, but expect walkers, runners and cyclists passing by.

pa_seldom_seen.blurb: Seldom Seen is an unusual urban crag in Pittsburgh's Seldom Seen Greenway, where climbers use old quarried-stone bridges, tunnel faces and retaining walls. Most routes are bolted sport lines, with one trad line, roughly 30 to 45 feet tall. The grade range runs from the mid 5.5s to the low 5.10s, and the bulk of the routes sit right at 5.9, a good fit for steady intermediates. The stone has seams between blocks and rounded pockets that climb a lot like natural rock. Water seeps through the cracks after wet weather, so the walls can be damp, and passersby on the greenway are common.
